checks: For a finite cover each positive intrinsic q-volume fiber is full-dimensional in its own affine span. Constant traces can be replaced for the local application by full or empty intersections of nonzero-normal intrinsic halfspaces, preserving all incidences and captured volumes. ac7ba1e1e0ebc955 then gives the pointwise surplus inequality at each nonnegative threshold.

The first weighted identity is an expansion of the surplus. For every label the strict comparison A_ai>alpha_i selects precisely the contributing bases, each contributing weight is at most L_a, and the sum of captured intrinsic fiber volumes is the original global cap mass.

At alpha_i=A_(3)i, tied masses and padded zero ranks leave exactly A_(1)i+A_(2)i−2A_(3)i as the positive-part sum. Kappa≥0 follows from the binomial bound including q=1. Grouping the ranked expression by original label gives both maxima and preserves the rank information in each fiber.

The finite polyhedral h-projection is closed, the objective is bounded below with bounded sublevels since h_i≥e_i≥0, and a constant height is feasible. For q>1 the objective extension is differentiable even at zero, while q=1 uses a linear objective. Feasible directions in the active linear constraints give the stated nonnegative KKT multipliers by finite Farkas.

The g_i stationarity and complementarity make the weighted outgoing height difference zero. Multiplying h-stationarity by h_i gives sum lambda_i e_i = q sum h_i^q. For q>1, a zero-height row sends only to zero heights; summing stationarity over that set gives zero obstacle multipliers and zero incoming flux from positive heights, so the division defining rho at positive lambda is legitimate. For q=1 the formula avoids division.

An independent exact actual example uses [−1,1]×[0,1] at each of z=−1,0,1 and caps x+z≤0 and x+z≥0. At q=2 the residual roots are (0,1,0), optimum heights are (1,1,1), and valid contact weights are (0,3,0). Thresholds (0,1,0) give E=(0,1/4,0), both loads zero, and both sides of the positive-part bound equal 27/4. This checks the strict-threshold tie convention and contact normalization.
